purpose: Teach: それ程/くるくる/エライ/終われ/あたたかい/はっと/通り越し/飛び出す

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはそれ程口数の多い方ではなかったぞ
lines.en: Your father wasn't much of a talker when he was younger, was he.
lines.style: Gentle, measured nostalgia. Soft attack. Eyes slightly distant. Warm but not sentimental — the tone of someone remembering a quiet truth. Slight upward lilt at the end, like he's inviting her into the memory rather than stating it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お孫様と一緒にくるくる回って踊られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: No — though he used to spin around dancing with the grandchildren, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Bright recall, almost playful. Warm lilt on 'grandchildren'. A small laugh caught in her voice. She's gently correcting him with affection, painting the picture as she speaks. Conversational, not corrective.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはエライご功績を残されたぞ
lines.en: Your father left quite a legacy when he was young, you know.
lines.style: Soft, deliberate. Each word carries weight. Quiet pride underneath. Pause after 'legacy' — he's weighing the memory. Not boastful, but respectful of what his father accomplished. Voice settles deeper.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お仕事を終われずに夜遅くまで残られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and he used to stay so late at the office, finishing his work. Remember, dear?
lines.style: Gently wistful, almost singing the memory. She's not complaining — she's painting it with tenderness. Voice softens on 'late' — acknowledgment of a small sacrifice made without complaint. A small, knowing smile in her tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんのあたたかいお言葉に救われたぞ
lines.en: When I was young, his warm words saved me more than once.
lines.style: Voice quiets on 'warm words'. Real vulnerability here — not performed, but genuinely moved by the memory. Slow pace. A slight catch, like the feeling is fresher than expected. Eyes likely closing slightly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の顔を見てはっと笑ってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh, and didn't he just light up when the grandchildren came home? His whole face would brighten.
lines.style: Warm, animated recall. Voice lifts on 'light up'. She's painting the picture vividly — present-tense in her memory. Small, genuine laugh. The rhythm picks up slightly, carried by the joy of that image. Affectionate address to him at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは予定を通り越して仕事に集中されたぞ
lines.en: He got so caught up in his work back then, lost all track of time.
lines.style: Quiet acceptance underneath wistfulness. Knowing tone — not complaint, but the tone of someone who understood his priorities and honored them. Slow, deliberate delivery. Slight shake of the head in affection, not judgment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様がお家を飛び出すように喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But oh, how he loved rushing home to see those grandchildren's faces. That joy — that was real.
lines.style: Voice brightens considerably on 'rushing home'. Almost tender-fierce on 'that joy'. She's defending him gently, painting a fuller picture. Rising warmth through the line. Slight tremor of genuine emotion at the end, like this is the truth that matters most.
